parents.subject: Food Science and Human Nutrition
parents.course: Advanced Topics in Food Science and Human Nutrition

ns2:section.sectionText: This course is devoted to learning the 1) physiological and psychological basis of human subjects, 2) chemistry of aroma and taste, 3) basic sensory methodologies in food evaluation, and 4) analysis and interpretation of sensory data. Recommended to have taken foundational statistics course, i.e., STAT 100, STAT 200 or FSHN 440. Lecture and lab instructional format. Graduate students will be required to do an extra project to earn graduate level credit of this FSHN 302 course.
ns2:section.sectionDeptRestriction: Restricted to students in the Food Science & Human Nutrition department.
